summary.short: Bill adding Virginia Code Chapter 58 (§§ 59.1-607 to 59.1-612) on high-risk AI systems used in consequential decisions. Imposes duties of care, documentation, impact assessments, consumer notice and appeal on developers and deployers, enforced by the Attorney General; effective July 1, 2026 if enacted.
summary.long: The bill would add Chapter 58, the High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Developer and Deployer Act, to Title 59.1 of the Code of Virginia. It covers developers and deployers doing business in the Commonwealth whose high-risk AI systems make, or are a substantial factor in making, consequential decisions such as education, employment, financial or lending services, health care, housing, insurance, legal services and parole. Developers must use a reasonable duty of care against algorithmic discrimination, provide documentation to deployers, and make outputs of high-risk generative AI systems identifiable, subject to exceptions. Deployers must maintain a risk management policy and program, complete impact assessments before initial deployment and before significant updates, retain records for three years, disclose AI use, give adverse-decision explanations, correction and appeal rights, and publish a statement on managing algorithmic discrimination risk. Exemptions cover, among others, certain federal, banking, insurance and health care actors. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority, with a 45-day cure opportunity, civil penalties of up to $1,000 for violations and $1,000 to $10,000 for willful violations, and no private right of action. The provisions take effect July 1, 2026.

notes: Text is the bill as supplied; no enrolled, chaptered or consolidated version and no legislative history appear in the document. The 'vetoed' status comes from registry metadata and is not stated in the text. Effective date (July 1, 2026) is from enacting clause 2 of the bill. Enacting clause 3 preserves existing causes of action, while § 59.1-611(I) states the chapter creates no private cause of action; both are coded as stated. Developer disclosure updates run 90 days after a modification (§ 59.1-608(G)) and deployer updates 30 days after notice (§ 59.1-609(F)); these are different duties, not a contradiction. Source typo: 'Federal Housing F inance Agency' in § 59.1-610(J). Section 59.1-609(C) runs its enumerated impact-assessment items inline in one paragraph.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes the legal treatment of any person in this bill. The only dollar amounts are civil penalty amounts in § 59.1-611(D), recorded under enforcement. The day periods (§ 59.1-608(G), § 59.1-609(F), § 59.1-611(G) and (H)), the three-year record retention period (§ 59.1-609(C)) and the July 1, 2026 effective date are procedural time limits or events. Scope is defined by the consequential-decision categories and the list of excluded technologies, not by numbers.
